selectionSummary: Selected by cross-border reach, gravity of harm or dependence, institutional scale, prospective enduring impact, and breadth of independent reporting, not by a claim of objectively ranking world events: COP31 negotiations, Ukraine's civilian and energy infrastructure under attack, and the global Microsoft 365 disruption.

snapshot.summary: The UN chief pressed COP31 negotiators for deep emissions cuts amid fossil-fuel disagreements; Russian strikes compounded Ukraine's civilian and power-grid vulnerabilities as diplomacy remained unsettled; and Microsoft 365 users worldwide experienced continued disruptions with partial service restoration.
connections: Energy security runs through climate negotiations and the wartime damage to Ukraine's electricity facilities, though the causes are unrelated.
The Microsoft outage and Ukraine's damaged power infrastructure illustrate different vulnerabilities of society-wide critical systems.
All three stories require separating official pledges, military assertions or company incident updates from independently established outcomes.
uncertainties: Final COP31 obligations on fossil fuels, clean electricity and adaptation finance remained unsettled.
Full war-zone casualty and drone counts, Ukraine grid recovery, and European security talks remained unresolved.
Microsoft's independently established root cause, global affected user count and complete restoration time remained unknown.

stories.title: Guterres urges emissions cuts as COP31 remains divided over fossil fuels and electrification
stories.summary: In Antalya, UN Secretary-General António Guterres urged immediate emissions reductions while COP31 governments remained divided about fossil-fuel commitments. A proposed global electrification target did not necessarily require that additional power be renewable. Climate-vulnerable nations pressed for adaptation finance. The first week ended without agreement on these central questions.
stories.whyItMatters: Power-sector investment, emissions policy and adaptation finance have multi-decade consequences for climate risk, economic growth, and communities most exposed to extreme weather.
stories.selectionRationale: A global intergovernmental summit governing the pace of emissions reductions and financing impacts populations, ecosystems and major economies across borders.
stories.evidenceNote: Reuters and AP independently report the secretary-general's November 13 intervention and disputed electrification terms; Guardian reports from the summit. Guardian was modified November 14 at 02:31 UTC, after cutoff: no authenticated historical snapshot exists and no unique later-only factual detail is treated as contemporaneous.

commonFacts.text: On November 13 at COP31 in Antalya, António Guterres publicly called for immediate and drastic emissions cuts.
The summit debated an electrification target whose text did not require all extra electricity to come from renewables.
Delegations were divided over language restricting fossil fuels and had not concluded a final summit agreement.

framingDifferences.text: Reuters frames the issue around negotiating blocs and energy-policy constraints; AP centers scientific urgency, clean-power tradeoffs and vulnerable-country financing.
Guardian stresses the UN's moral and political responsibility for climate justice, compared with Reuters' emphasis on the mechanics of state negotiations.

uncertainties: Whether an enforceable fossil-fuel transition clause would be agreed in the final summit text.
Whether electrification commitments would mandate low-carbon generation and what adaptation funding would be delivered.
Guardian's exact pre-cutoff text is not archived; the report was modified after cutoff.

stories.title: Russian attacks damage a Kyiv hospital as Ukraine struggles to restore power plants
stories.summary: Russian attacks damaged a hospital in Kyiv on November 13, while energy workers raced to repair power stations shattered in earlier strikes ahead of winter. Russia asserted it had downed almost 1,200 Ukrainian drones overnight, a claim reported but not independently established. US-led discussions about Ukraine and wider European security continued without a settlement.
stories.whyItMatters: Damage to electricity and heating systems threatens civilian survival in winter, while military escalation and unsettled European security diplomacy create significant regional and international risks.
stories.selectionRationale: Large-scale war, civilian casualties, winter energy security and negotiations touching NATO and wider Europe give the development major near-term and enduring consequences.
stories.evidenceNote: Reuters directly visited damaged DTEK power infrastructure; Guardian reported from a Kyiv hospital; AP independently covered cross-border raids and European diplomacy. The Russian nearly-1,200-drone tally and Ukrainian Starshield complaints are explicitly attributed. Guardian page was modified after historical cutoff without a retained snapshot.

stories.title: Global Microsoft 365 outage disrupts business and public services into a second day
stories.summary: Outlook, Teams, Copilot and other Microsoft 365 services experienced serious disruptions across countries on November 12 and 13. Reports from the user-driven Downdetector tracker came from 74 countries and territories, but did not measure the total number of people affected. Microsoft reported gradual recovery and said it had no indication of a cyberattack. Independent root-cause findings and global restoration timing remained unconfirmed by cutoff.
stories.whyItMatters: Communications, healthcare, government and commerce rely on a small set of cloud platforms, making systemic service failures transnational risks and raising questions about redundancy and digital sovereignty.
stories.selectionRationale: Documented disruption reports across 74 countries and effects on government, healthcare and businesses created exceptionally broad, direct economic and institutional exposure.
stories.evidenceNote: AP, Al Jazeera and Guardian publish separately bylined original reporting and explore different questions. Guardian article first appeared November 12 and was updated November 13 before cutoff. Downdetector reports are user submissions, not a census. Microsoft technical explanations are attributed, not independent root-cause proof.

commonFacts.text: Microsoft 365 platforms including Outlook and Teams experienced worldwide disruptions from November 12 continuing into November 13.
Downdetector had received self-reported service complaints from 74 countries or territories; that does not establish the number of customers affected.
On November 13 Microsoft announced that restoration was progressing while some customers were still experiencing problems.

framingDifferences.text: AP stresses risks of dependence on a single technology provider; Al Jazeera focuses on explaining the multi-region outage and limited technical certainty.
Guardian emphasizes disruption to British public services and recovery operations, compared with AP's broader concentration and sovereignty analysis.

uncertainties: An independently confirmed technical root cause was not available by cutoff.
Total affected user counts and the final worldwide service-restoration time were unknown.
Microsoft's denial of cyberattack involvement was a company assertion, not proof from an independent investigation.

unverifiedClaims.text: Microsoft said the disruptions had no indication of cyberattack or AI agent involvement and were related to a technical infrastructure problem.
unverifiedClaims.reason: Independent reporting establishes that Microsoft gave these explanations; no independent technical forensic finding was reviewed.

review.note: ChatGPT opened and read nine originating newsroom pages, checked headlines, dates, bylines, genres, full URLs and anonymous free access, independently corroborated AP original calendar dates from contemporary AP distribution, and checked each common fact against at least two selected sources.
